messages:
alex: heads-up — hit a bug with the python async client retrying a POST and creating duplicate records in prod.
marisol: oh no. quick summary?
alex: flow: user calls client.create_document(...) without an idempotency key, server 502 during commit, client auto-retries and server processed the first request before failing — ended up with duplicate documents.
ben: is this the streaming/async path or sync?
alex: async only so far — httpx + our RetryMiddleware. It retries on 502/503/504 by default.
katie: iirc we add a new uuid idempotency token in middleware on retry? or do we preserve original?
alex: that is the thing — we were generating a new Idempotency-Key for the retried call (bad). So the server treats it as a fresh create.
marisol: wow. so middleware mutated headers on retry instead of copying original. bug.
ben: reason it slipped: most endpoints are safe to replay (GET/PUT) but POST creates are not. Need to either preserve original idempotency key or avoid replaying non-idempotent requests.
katie: proposed fixes?
alex: two options: (1) always preserve the original Idempotency-Key header when retrying; (2) if no key provided, do NOT auto-replay non-idempotent verbs (POST/PATCH/DELETE with side-effects) — require explicit opt-in.
marisol: (1) is straightforward but only helps if caller set a key. Generating one for them silently still risks uniqueness per attempt if we accidentally regen. But if we auto-generate at first send and preserve on retries that's reasonable.
ben: agree. generate on first send and store in request.context so retry reuses it. But also need docs about when to set your own key.
katie: another concern: streaming completions/cancelled streams. If you cancel mid-stream client cancels connection, server might have created resource already. We should not auto-retry cancelled streams.
alex: yep. added to bug notes: don't replay on client-side cancellations; preserve original key between attempts; add opt-in config on client: retry_on_server_errors_for_non_idempotent: bool = False by default.
marisol: typing/SDK parity notes: signature change for create_document should accept idempotency_key: Optional[str] = None and we need to update typed stubs + mypy tests. Use PEP604 union for py>=3.10 but keep typing.Optional for py3.9 support.
ben: tests?
alex: wrote unit tests using respx + httpx for async flow to assert header preserved and only one resource created. Also an integration smoke test for Dedicated that simulates a 502 after commit.
katie: also update sample-app onboarding doc to show how to pass idempotency_key and rationale — onboarding friction caused a lot of this.
marisol: what about backoff tuning? folks saw immediate retry (0s) followed by exponential. Should we add jitter and a minimum backoff of 50-100ms for create operations?
ben: add config: backoff_base_ms, backoff_multiplier, max_jitter_ms. Default base 100, multiplier 2, jitter 50. Also cap total retry window.
alex: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 (draft) — includes: preserve idempotency token, generate on first send, opt-in flag for non-idempotent replay, streaming cancel guard, typing updates, tests, docs.
katie: nice. can we also surface a runtime warning when a non-idempotent request is retried without an explicit key? so users see it in dev.
marisol: good idea — logger.warning with a link to docs.
ben: deployment plan? can we gate behavior behind feature flag to avoid surprises?
alex: plan: merge tests + types first, roll with opt-in disabled (safe), then enable auto-generate-and-preserve behavior behind minor-version release and extensive canary on staging + Dedicated.
katie: assign reviewers: @marisol for runtime, @ben for tests, @alex for docs.
retry-bot: CI: unit-tests passed (python3.10, py3.11), integration-smoke failed on first run (timeout) — rerunning.
alex: thanks — will update changelog and sample-app. Also adding explicit note in quickstart about idempotency best-practices to reduce onboarding tickets.
marisol: awesome. can we also add a lint rule to prevent middleware from mutating headers on retry? catch via a test harness.
ben: yeah add contract test that ensures headers preserved across retries unless explicit regeneration function provided.
alex: ok i'll iterate on PR per feedback and post an update later today. :thumbsup:
katie: thanks alex — big one avoided. everyone, please skim the PR when it's up. :eyes:
